what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Unexplained agent bills are an engineering defect to fix
sections.para: A business plan for a service that helps companies manage agentic AI cost by observing what already exists. Agents shipped from the explorer side, with logs and invoices nobody reads together and no cost owner. The service installs nothing, builds footprints, a twin and policies, and returns two lists: what to stop paying for and what to build.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Existing logs, read together, yield cost and build lists
sections.para: Unexplained bills come from estates grown in sessions without policy, twin, owner or cap. Invoices, traces and prompts read together give each agent a footprint. The service returns a cost list and an engineering list, treats missing data as findings, moves data through vaults, and offers four price levels plus a share-of-savings option.

sections.label: The problem, on a map
sections.line: Agents built as explorers run on commodities nobody reconciles
sections.para: Agents usually grow from a session prompt into production, the explorer side of the map, while running on commodity model APIs billed exactly. Invoices, logs and traces exist but nobody reads them together, and no one owns cost. Loops, whole-context calls and keys without ceilings are defects engineers fix once visible.

sections.label: What the service does
sections.line: Observe, map footprint, twin and policy, then find savings
sections.para: Customers drop invoices, traces, prompts and schedules into their own sealed vault. The service builds each agent's footprint, a twin of the estate with cost on every edge, and the policy each agent actually ran under. It then lists savings, such as context cut by ninety per cent, and engineering opportunities.

sections.label: Why the positive frame matters
sections.line: Sell cost reduction, deliver engineering opportunity
sections.para: A cost review is bought once and resented; a map of what to build brings customers back. The same logs that show a loop show the workflow worth building, and shared prompts reveal missing components. Gaps such as unlogged agents or unowned keys are the first findings most companies need.

sections.label: Why vaults
sections.line: Vaults fit capture, transformation and movement of the data
sections.para: Customers encrypt logs into a vault they own and can revoke, and the service holds only a read key. Every step from invoice to finding is a commit, so findings trace back to source lines. Anonymised extracts leave as sealed envelopes to a benchmark vault, after the customer sees them.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.line: Four price levels from £50 to Tailored, all assumptions
sections.para: The kit costs £50, a self-run cost vault £250, a Standard estate read £3,000 within ten working days, and Tailored from £9,000, with a share-of-savings alternative. About eight Standard and two Tailored engagements a month would cover a two-founder burn. Every number is a labelled assumption.

sections.label: What is already here, and what is not
sections.line: The methods exist; parsers, catalogue and customers do not
sections.para: The footprint method, behaviour policy format, connector twin design, vault tooling, sealed envelopes and Company X-Ray pattern already exist. Missing are the cost analysis catalogue, the agent estate twin schema, log parsers, the benchmark vault and any customer. That is a few weeks of work.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: No estate read yet; prices and map are sketches
sections.para: The two lists describe what is expected, not found, and the prices are assumptions to test on the first three customers. The Wardley map is an argument, not a measurement. Share of savings needs an invoice baseline and agreed attribution before anyone signs.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: a voice memo and earlier site articles
sections.para: Written from a 12 October 2026 voice memo after a conversation with an unnamed potential collaborator. It builds on Footprint and blast radius, The behaviour policy is the business logic, Connector Twin, The agent is the reader, Every mistake added a rule, RFC 0001 and the business plans page.
